purpose: Repaint the older islam films reused in wave 1 so each has its own look (owner: "We can't have the same look for every film").
neighbours: new month-one Muslim films: 29 inkwash, 30 riso
rules: Absolutely no people in this picture: no human figures, silhouettes, faces, prophets or angels. Show only landscape, architecture, objects, animals, nature and light. No Arabic or any other writing.
today shots: Show only hands (no face, no full body) of a modern person. No Arabic or any other writing.
each shot keeps its story beat and framing (the old still is uploaded as a layout guide); only the look changes

films.suffix: Moroccan zellige and Persian tilework: geometric star patterns, cobalt and turquoise glaze, sunlight through carved screens, glossy tiles, architecture and nature only

shots.name: BM1-Mountain-Of-Light
shots.beat: Near Mecca, high on a bare mountain, is a small cave called Hira. Before his calling, Muhammad ﷺ often went there alone to pray.

shots.name: BM2-The-Cave
shots.beat: Then, in the cave, the angel Jibril came to him with one word: “Read!”

shots.name: BM3-Read
shots.beat: “I am not a reader,” he said. Three times the command came. Then the first words: “Read in the name of your Lord, who created.”

shots.name: BM4-Home-Lamp
shots.beat: He hurried home, shaking, and said to his wife Khadijah, “Cover me, cover me.” She wrapped him up and stayed beside him.

shots.name: BM5-Reed-Pen
shots.beat: “God will never disgrace you,” she told him. “You are good to your family, you carry the weak, you welcome guests.” She stood by him from the very start.

shots.name: BM6-Today-First-Bite
shots.beat: today scene, today first bite: before the next thing you start today, a meal, a message, the car, say “bismillah,” out loud or under your breath. or just give it one full pause.

films.suffix: Persian stained-glass window light (orosi): jewel-toned coloured glass in geometric wooden lattice, sunbeams throwing coloured light across tiles and carpet

shots.name: FA1-Palm-Mosque
shots.beat: In the simple mosque in Medina, roofed with palm branches, a man named Abu Sa‘id was praying when the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ called his name.

shots.name: FA2-Prayer-Mat
shots.beat: He finished his prayer, then came over. The Prophet ﷺ told him, “Before you leave the mosque, I will teach you the greatest surah, the greatest chapter, of the Qur’an.”

shots.name: FA3-The-Door
shots.beat: They walked toward the door together. Just before they reached it, Abu Sa‘id spoke up: “You said you would teach me.”

shots.name: FA4-Seven-Lamps
shots.beat: “Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,” he answered. “It is the seven oft-repeated verses.” Al-Fatiha: the opening.

shots.name: FA5-Dawn-Prayer-Today
shots.beat: today scene, dawn prayer today: pick one line of al-Fatiha and learn what it means: “show us the straight path.” it’s your choice: just read it, listen for it when someone prays, or say it yourself.

shots.name: FA6-Learning-Today
shots.beat: today scene, learning today: pick one line of al-Fatiha and learn what it means: “show us the straight path.” it’s your choice: just read it, listen for it when someone prays, or say it yourself.

films.suffix: a loose watercolour and black ink wash on white paper: bleeding pigment, confident black ink linework, lots of white paper, one or two bold colours

shots.name: WU1-Medina-Dawn
shots.beat: In Medina lived a man named Bilal. He had once been enslaved. Freed, he became the one who called people to prayer, his voice carrying over the roofs at dawn.

shots.name: WU2-After-Dawn-Prayer
shots.beat: One morning after the dawn prayer, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ turned to him: “Bilal, I heard your footsteps ahead of me in paradise. What have you been doing?”

shots.name: WU3-Water-Jug
shots.beat: Bilal answered, “The deed I hope in most is this: whenever I make wudu, by day or by night, I pray with it.” Wudu is the washing before prayer.

shots.name: WU4-Water-Over-Hands
shots.beat: The washing itself comes from one verse of the Qur’an: wash the face, and the arms up to the elbows, wipe the head, then the feet.

shots.name: WU5-Water-Runs-Off
shots.beat: And a saying of the Prophet ﷺ pictures it: as the water runs off the face, the hands and the feet, the wrongs they did run off with it.

shots.name: WU6-Row-Of-Taps-Today
shots.beat: today scene, row of taps today: learn the order of wudu from the verse today: face, arms to the elbows, a wipe over the head, then the feet. those are the steps the verse names; a teacher can show you the whole of wudu, which begi

films.suffix: a two- or three-colour risograph poster print: bold flat shapes, slightly misregistered ink, halftone dots, lime, black and hot pink

shots.name: IN1-Two-Gardens
shots.beat: The Qur’an tells of a man with two gardens, heavy with grapes, ringed with date palms, a stream running between them.

shots.name: IN2-Proud-Walk
shots.beat: He walked through them with a friend and said, “I don’t think this will ever end.”

shots.name: IN3-The-Gate
shots.beat: His friend asked: when you came into your garden, why didn’t you say, “Ma sha’ Allah,” what God has willed? There is no strength except in God.

shots.name: IN4-Fallen-Vines
shots.beat: Then the harvest was struck down. The vines fell onto their trellises, and the man wrung his hands over everything he had spent.

shots.name: IN5-Tomorrow
shots.beat: In the same chapter, the Qur’an says: never say of anything, “I will do it tomorrow,” without adding, “if God wills.” In sha’ Allah.

shots.name: IN6-Today-New-Baby
shots.beat: today scene, today new baby: today, when you talk about a plan, add “if God wills,” even quietly. and when you see something good, say “mashallah,” or just name it as a gift.

films.suffix: neon night photography, a real photo not a painting: wet surfaces, magenta, lime and electric-blue neon glow, deep black shadows, long-exposure light trails, cinematic grain

shots.name: DB1-One-Star
shots.beat: The Qur’an tells how Ibrahim, Abraham, looked up one night and saw a bright star. “This is my Lord,” he said. Then the star set.

shots.name: DB2-Moonrise
shots.beat: “I don’t love things that set,” he said. Then the moon rose, shining. “This is my Lord.” But the moon set too.

shots.name: DB3-Sunrise
shots.beat: Then the sun came up, bigger than all of them. “This is greater.” And it set. So he turned to the One who made the heavens and the earth.

shots.name: DB4-Four-Hills
shots.beat: Later, the Qur’an says, he asked God: “Show me how You give life to the dead.” “Don’t you believe?” “Yes, but so that my heart may be at ease.”

shots.name: DB5-Night-Lamp
shots.beat: Centuries later, some companions told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ they had thoughts too troubling to say aloud. “That,” he told them, “is clear faith.”

shots.name: DB6-Today-Late-Night
shots.beat: today scene, today late night: if there’s a question you’ve been carrying, write it down tonight, or bring it to an imam or someone you trust. and if a night question ever comes with real darkness, please reach out: 988 in the US,

shots.name: RA1-Palm-Grove
shots.beat: In the early days of the fast in Medina, the rule was stricter: if you fell asleep after sunset before eating, no more food until the next sunset.

shots.name: RA2-Sunset-House
shots.beat: A man named Qays worked all day in his palm grove, fasting. At sunset he came home, and his wife went out to find him some food.

shots.name: RA3-Sleeping-Mat
shots.beat: Worn out, he fell asleep before she came back. So he fasted on through the next day, and by midday he fainted.

shots.name: RA4-Two-Threads
shots.beat: Then a verse came: eat and drink through the night, until the white thread of dawn shows clear from the black thread of night.

shots.name: RA5-Pillow-Threads
shots.beat: One man named ‘Adi took it literally. He put a white thread and a black thread under his pillow, and kept checking all night. He couldn’t tell them apart.

shots.name: RA6-Iftar-Today
shots.beat: today scene, iftar today: try a small fast of the tongue today: no sharp or untrue word until sunset. when one comes up, let it go, the way the fast lets the food go.

films.suffix: a Y2K chrome 3D render: liquid-metal surfaces, iridescent highlights, glossy bubble shapes, silver and lime reflections

shots.name: EI1-Medina-Oasis
shots.beat: When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to Medina, the people there kept two old yearly days of games and celebration.

shots.name: EI2-New-Crescent
shots.beat: “God has given you two better days,” he said: the day of sacrifice, and the day of breaking the fast. The two Eids.

shots.name: EI3-Food-For-All
shots.beat: Eid al-Fitr comes when Ramadan ends. Before its prayer, every family gives food for each person in it, so people in need can feast too.

shots.name: EI4-Night-Of-The-Dream
shots.beat: Eid al-Adha, the day of sacrifice, remembers a story in the Qur’an. Ibrahim dreamed he must sacrifice his son, and asked the boy what he thought.

shots.name: EI5-Ram-At-Dawn
shots.beat: “Father, do as you are told,” his son said. “God willing, you’ll find me patient.” Then a voice called out, and a great sacrifice was given in the boy’s place.

shots.name: EI6-Eid-Morning-Today
shots.beat: today scene, eid morning today: think of one person who might not have a feast this season. share a meal, a plate or a small gift with them this week, the way eid makes room for everyone.

films.suffix: a layered paper cut-out collage: cut and torn coloured paper, visible paper fibres, soft drop shadows, handmade diorama depth, bright lime, pink, saffron and turquoise paper

shots.name: SM1-First-Garden
shots.beat: A saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells that when God created Adam, the first human, He said to him: go and greet that gathering of angels.

shots.name: SM2-Circle-Of-Light
shots.beat: “Listen to how they answer you,” God told him. “That will be your greeting, and your children’s greeting.”

shots.name: SM3-Light-Returns
shots.beat: Adam said, “As-salamu alaykum,” peace be upon you. The angels answered, “Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God.”

shots.name: SM4-Quran-Stand
shots.beat: The Qur’an makes it a rule: when someone greets you, answer with something better, or at least give the same back.

shots.name: SM5-Medina-Lanes
shots.beat: The Prophet ﷺ told his companions: you won’t truly believe until you love one another. And what grows that love? Spread salaam among yourselves.

shots.name: SM6-Airport-Today
shots.beat: today scene, airport today: today, greet one person first, before they greet you. a saying teaches that the one who greets first is nearest to God. say “salaam” if it fits, or wish them peace in your own words. and when someone gr

shots.name: PL1-Medina-Mosque
shots.beat: ‘Umar remembered a day in Medina, sitting with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, when a stranger walked in, his clothes brilliant white, his hair very black.

shots.name: PL2-White-Light-Door
shots.beat: There was no dust of travel on him, yet no one knew him. He sat knee to knee with the Prophet ﷺ and asked, “Tell me about Islam.”

shots.name: PL3-Five-Pillars
shots.beat: Bear witness that there is no god but God and Muhammad is His messenger. Pray. Give zakat. Fast Ramadan. Make the pilgrimage, if you are able.

shots.name: PL4-Empty-Mats
shots.beat: He asked about faith, and about worshipping God as if you see Him, then left. It was the angel Jibril, the Prophet ﷺ said, come to teach them their religion.

shots.name: PL5-Kaaba-Today
shots.beat: today scene, kaaba today: today, learn the five by name, one on each finger: shahada, salat, zakat, sawm, hajj. then, if you like, ask a muslim friend which pillar holds them up most.

shots.name: PL6-Home-Dawn-Today
shots.beat: today scene, home dawn today: today, learn the five by name, one on each finger: shahada, salat, zakat, sawm, hajj. then, if you like, ask a muslim friend which pillar holds them up most.

shots.name: NJ1-Mecca-Night
shots.beat: One night, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells, he was taken from Mecca to Jerusalem, and from there up through the heavens.

shots.name: NJ3-Heavens-Opening
shots.beat: There, God gave him a gift for his people: fifty prayers, every day.

shots.name: NJ4-Light-Descending
shots.beat: He went back, and the number came down. Musa sent him again, and again, until it was five.

shots.name: NJ5-Five-Suns
shots.beat: “They are five,” God said, “and they are fifty.” Five prayers a day, with the reward of fifty.

shots.name: NJ6-Stockroom-Today
shots.beat: today scene, stockroom today: today, notice where the sun is at five moments: before sunrise, after midday, afternoon, sunset, night. it’s your choice: just notice, look up the prayer times where you live, or try one slow bow your

shots.name: TS1-Medina-Room
shots.beat: One day, two men were sitting near the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Then both of them sneezed.

shots.name: TS2-Dust-In-Light
shots.beat: To one he said, “Yarhamuk Allah,” may God have mercy on you. To the other, nothing. The other man asked him why.

shots.name: TS3-Office-Sneeze-Today
shots.beat: today scene, office sneeze today: today, say “alhamdulillah,” or “praise be to God,” once on purpose for something good, and once for something hard. or, if you’d rather, just name both and let them belong to the same day.

shots.name: TS4-Sun-And-Rain
shots.beat: Hamd, praise, isn’t quite shukr, thanks. Thanks answers a good thing done for you. Praise answers who someone is, on any kind of day.

shots.name: TS5-Grandmother-Today
shots.beat: today scene, grandmother today: today, say “alhamdulillah,” or “praise be to God,” once on purpose for something good, and once for something hard. or, if you’d rather, just name both and let them belong to the same day.

shots.name: TS6-Beads-Today
shots.beat: today scene, beads today: today, say “alhamdulillah,” or “praise be to God,” once on purpose for something good, and once for something hard. or, if you’d rather, just name both and let them belong to the same day.

films.suffix: a heavy impasto oil painting: thick palette-knife strokes you can feel, deep black-blue shadows, blazing highlights, dramatic chiaroscuro

shots.name: DW1-Desert-Well
shots.beat: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once told of a man walking a desert road. He grew so thirsty that he climbed down into a well and drank.

shots.name: DW2-Thirsty-Dog
shots.beat: When he climbed out, he saw a dog, panting, licking the damp earth because it was so thirsty.

shots.name: DW3-Leather-Sock
shots.beat: “This dog is as thirsty as I was,” he thought. He climbed down again, filled his leather sock, held it in his teeth, and climbed up.

shots.name: DW4-Dog-Drinks
shots.beat: He gave the dog water. And God thanked him for it, the Prophet ﷺ said, and forgave him.

shots.name: DW5-Every-World
shots.beat: “Is there reward for us even with animals?” the companions asked. “In every living thing,” he said, “there is reward.”

shots.name: DW6-Water-Bowl-Today
shots.beat: today scene, water bowl today: today, put out a little water for something that lives near you: a bowl by the door, a dish for the birds, a plant that’s gone dry. a small share in tending the worlds.

films.suffix: a glittering gold-tessera mosaic: small stone and glass tiles, blazing gold ground, deep cobalt and crimson, flat sacred composition

shots.name: MC1-Camp-At-Dawn
shots.beat: One day, captives were brought before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Among them, a mother was rushing from child to child, searching.

shots.name: MC2-Shawl-In-Wind
shots.beat: Whenever she found a baby among them, she pulled it close to her and fed it.

shots.name: MC3-Held-Close
shots.beat: The Prophet ﷺ turned to his companions. “Could this woman ever throw her own child into a fire?” “No,” they said, “not if she could help it.”

shots.name: MC4-Mare-And-Foal
shots.beat: Another saying: God made mercy in a hundred parts, and sent one part into the world. With it, a mare lifts her hoof so she won’t hurt her foal.

shots.name: MC5-One-Part
shots.beat: And when God finished creating, a saying tells, He wrote in a book kept with Him: “My mercy outstrips My anger.”

shots.name: MC6-Arrivals-Today
shots.beat: today scene, arrivals today: a saying teaches: be merciful to those on earth, and the One above will be merciful to you. so today, show one mercy past what’s owed: a patient reply, a second chance, a call to someone hard to love.

films.suffix: a high-fashion editorial photograph, real models not a painting: sculptural styled wardrobe, dark seamless backdrop, a single hard spotlight, medium-format crispness, magazine-cover drama

shots.name: LG1-Old-Market
shots.beat: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told of a merchant, long ago, who lent money to people. When a debt came due and someone couldn’t pay, he did something unusual.

shots.name: LG2-Closed-Ledger
shots.beat: Every prayer, right after the two names of mercy, says: “Owner of the Day of Judgment.” Din means repayment, what each is due. Its root also gives dayn, debt.

shots.name: LG3-Coins-Returned
shots.beat: “Let it go,” he told his helpers. “Maybe God will let us go too.”

shots.name: LG4-Dawn-Plain
shots.beat: When his account was called, a saying tells, nothing good was found in it, except this one habit of letting debts go.

shots.name: LG5-Dishes-Today
shots.beat: today scene, dishes today: the qur’an says that letting a struggling person’s debt go, as charity, is better for you. so today, let one small debt go: a favor owed, a coffee never paid back, a small grudge. leave the account with

shots.name: LG6-Deleted-Text-Today
shots.beat: today scene, deleted text today: the qur’an says that letting a struggling person’s debt go, as charity, is better for you. so today, let one small debt go: a favor owed, a coffee never paid back, a small grudge. leave the account

shots.name: QAH1-Noon-Sand
shots.beat: In Mecca’s early years, a man named Bilal was enslaved. He had become a Muslim, and the man who owned him wanted him to take it back.

shots.name: QAH2-Heavy-Rock
shots.beat: The early biographies say he was made to lie on the hot sand at noon, with a heavy rock placed on his chest. “Give it up,” they told him.

shots.name: QAH3-Evening-Star
shots.beat: He said only one word, again and again. “Ahad. Ahad.” One. One. Later, Abu Bakr, a friend of the Prophet ﷺ, bought him and set him free.

shots.name: QAH4-Mosque-Turn
shots.beat: His word sits inside the prayer too. After four lines about God, al-Fatiha turns and speaks to Him: “You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help.”

shots.name: QAH5-One-Lamp
shots.beat: In the Arabic, “You” comes first: iyyaka na‘budu, You we worship. Putting it first means only You. The word for that is tawhid, making one.

shots.name: QAH6-Desk-Today
shots.beat: today scene, desk today: today, try one small tawhid moment. when something tugs hard at you, a deadline, a worry, a screen, say quietly: “real, but not God.” if you pray, you can rest one word there, as bilal did: ahad.

films.suffix: a single graphic-novel comic panel: bold black inks, halftone shading, dynamic camera angle, strong flat colour, no speech bubbles, no lettering

shots.name: QPA1-Sand-Courtyard
shots.beat: A companion named Ibn Mas‘ud remembered a day when the Prophet ﷺ sat with them and began to draw in the sand.

shots.name: QPA2-Straight-Line
shots.beat: First he drew one straight line. “This is the path of God,” he said.

shots.name: QPA3-Branching-Lines
shots.beat: Then lines to the right and left. “These are paths,” he said, “and on each one is a shaytan, a tempter, calling to it.”

shots.name: QPA4-Desert-Road
shots.beat: Then he recited from the Qur’an: “This is My straight path, so follow it, and don’t follow other ways, or they will scatter you.”

shots.name: QPA5-Gift-Lamp
shots.beat: Ihdina, show us, guide us, comes from the root h-d-y. The same root gives hadiya, a gift. Guidance is something handed to you.

shots.name: QPA6-Lost-Street-Today
shots.beat: today scene, lost street today: today, before one choice, big or small, ask the question al-fatiha asks: which way? many muslims pause on that line in prayer: ihdina s-sirata l-mustaqim, show us the straight path. it’s your choice

shots.name: QAD1-Medina-Lanes
shots.beat: When the Muslims first came to Medina, there was no call to prayer. People gathered by guessing the time.

shots.name: QAD2-Bell-Horn-Fire
shots.beat: So they talked it over. Ring a bell, as the Christians did? Blow a horn, as the Jews did? Light a fire?

shots.name: QAD3-Dream-Night
shots.beat: ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd dreamed of a man carrying a bell. Instead of selling it, the man taught him words: Allahu akbar, God is greatest.

shots.name: QAD4-Rooftop-Dawn
shots.beat: In the morning he told the Prophet ﷺ. “It is a true dream,” he said. “Teach it to Bilal. His voice carries further.”

shots.name: QAD5-Minarets-Today
shots.beat: today scene, minarets today: today, listen to one adhan, from a nearby mosque, a recording, or a prayer app. it’s your choice: just listen, learn the first line, or repeat it softly after the caller, as many muslims do.

shots.name: QAD6-Kitchen-Phone-Today
shots.beat: today scene, kitchen phone today: today, listen to one adhan, from a nearby mosque, a recording, or a prayer app. it’s your choice: just listen, learn the first line, or repeat it softly after the caller, as many muslims do.

shots.name: QJM1-Friday-Mosque
shots.beat: One Friday in Medina, the Prophet ﷺ stood giving the weekly sermon, and the mosque was full.

shots.name: QJM2-Caravan-Arrives
shots.beat: Then a caravan arrived from the north, camels heavy with food, and a sound of drums at the edge of town.

shots.name: QJM3-Mats-Left
shots.beat: People slipped out, one after another, until only twelve were left with him.

shots.name: QJM4-Lamp-Over-Grain
shots.beat: The Qur’an named it: when they see trade or amusement, they rush to it and leave you standing. Say: what is with God is better.

shots.name: QJM5-Street-Prayer-Today
shots.beat: today scene, street prayer today: a saying teaches there’s an hour on friday when a sincere prayer is answered. so today, find out when the friday prayer is at a mosque near you. it’s your choice: just look it up, visit and watch

shots.name: QJM6-Back-To-Work-Today
shots.beat: today scene, back to work today: a saying teaches there’s an hour on friday when a sincere prayer is answered. so today, find out when the friday prayer is at a mosque near you. it’s your choice: just look it up, visit and watch q

shots.name: QZK1-Three-Huts
shots.beat: The Prophet ﷺ told of three poor men, long ago: one with a skin disease people shrank from, one bald, and one blind.

shots.name: QZK2-Three-Valleys
shots.beat: Years passed. The first had a valley full of camels, the second a valley of cows, the third a valley of sheep.

shots.name: QZK3-Staff-At-Gate
shots.beat: The first two said no. “I have many costs,” they said, and “I inherited all this.” They had forgotten where it came from.

shots.name: QZK4-Open-Fold
shots.beat: The third said: “I was blind, and God gave me back my sight. Take whatever you want.” “Keep it,” the angel said. “You were only being tested.”

shots.name: QZK5-Pruned-Vine
shots.beat: That’s the heart of zakat. Its root, z-k-w, means both to purify and to grow. Like pruning a vine: cut some away, and what’s left grows better.

shots.name: QZK6-Kitchen-Table-Today
shots.beat: today scene, kitchen table today: today, try the third man’s memory. name one thing you have that was given to you, a skill, a home, someone’s help, and pass a small share of it on: a donation, a meal, an hour. if you’re curious,

shots.name: QAM1-Kaaba-Rebuilt
shots.beat: Long ago in Mecca, the clans rebuilt the Ka‘ba, the old house of worship. When it came to setting the sacred Black Stone back, they nearly came to blows.

shots.name: QAM2-Cloak-Stone
shots.beat: He spread out a cloak, set the stone in the middle, and asked a man from each clan to take a corner. Together they lifted it.

shots.name: QAM3-Safa-Hill
shots.beat: Years later, he climbed the hill of Safa and called the clans together. “If I told you riders in the valley were about to attack you, would you believe me?”

shots.name: QAM4-Valley-Below
shots.beat: “Yes,” they said. “We have never known you to lie.” Then he gave them his message, and many turned away.

shots.name: QAM5-Chest-Of-Valuables
shots.beat: Even so, the early biographies say, many who refused his message still left their valuables in his care. Trusted first. Believed, by many, only later.

shots.name: QAM6-Spare-Key-Today
shots.beat: today scene, spare key today: today, keep one small promise you’ve been putting off: the call, the book to return, the message you said you’d send. the qur’an praises those who keep their trusts and their promises, and al-amin was

shots.name: QIK1-Desert-Camp
shots.beat: The Prophet ﷺ once sent a man to lead a small expedition. Each time he led their prayer, he ended his recitation the same way.

shots.name: QIK2-Prayer-Rows
shots.beat: With one short surah, four lines long: “Say: He is God, the One.” Every single time.

shots.name: QIK3-Returning-Road
shots.beat: “Ask him why he does it,” the Prophet ﷺ said. The man answered: “Because it describes the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.”

shots.name: QIK4-Mountain-Path
shots.beat: It sits near the very end of the Qur’an, in its last thirtieth, juz’ ‘amma, where the short surahs are. That’s where almost everyone starts.

shots.name: QIK5-Grandmother-Child-Today

shots.name: QKH1-Heavens-Lights
shots.beat: The first story doesn’t start on earth. It starts in a conversation. God tells the angels: “I am placing a steward on the earth.”

shots.name: QKH2-Young-Earth
shots.beat: The angels ask: “Will You place there one who will cause harm and shed blood, while we praise You?”

shots.name: QKH3-Sweet-Green
shots.beat: God doesn’t scold them. He says only: “I know what you do not know.”

shots.name: QKH4-Garden-Gate
shots.beat: The word is khalifah: one who stands in for another. Not the owner of the garden. The one it’s entrusted to.

shots.name: QKH5-Sapling-Today
shots.beat: today scene, sapling today: today, tend one small piece of the trust: water a street tree, pick up litter on your block, or turn off what doesn’t need to be on. a saying teaches that whatever a bird or person eats from what you pl

shots.name: QNM1-Things-In-Light
shots.beat: Yesterday the angels asked why. Now God answers, not with an argument, but a test. He sets things before them: “Tell Me their names.”

shots.name: QNM2-Lights-Bowed
shots.beat: The angels answer honestly: “Glory be to You. We know nothing except what You have taught us.”

shots.name: QNM3-Things-Named
shots.beat: God had taught Adam all the names. “Adam, tell them,” He said. And Adam named them, one by one.

shots.name: QNM4-Bowl-And-Pot
shots.beat: What were the names? The Qur’an doesn’t say. One early scholar said everything, down to a bowl and a cooking pot.

shots.name: QNM5-Toddler-Today
shots.beat: today scene, toddler today: today, learn one name you’ve walked past: a tree on your street, a bird at the window, the name of the person who makes your coffee. if you like, add the qur’an’s short prayer: rabbi zidni ‘ilma, my Lor

shots.name: QIB1-Lights-Bowing
shots.beat: God told the angels to bow before Adam, the first human. And they bowed, every one of them.

shots.name: QIB2-One-Flame
shots.beat: All except Iblis. Elsewhere the Qur’an says he was of the jinn, beings made of fire. “What kept you from bowing?” God asked.

shots.name: QIB3-Fire-And-Clay
shots.beat: “I am better than him,” Iblis said. “You made me from fire, and him from clay.”

shots.name: QIB4-Flame-Path
shots.beat: What held him back wasn’t hunger or fear. It was a comparison. Pride, the first wrong in the story.

shots.name: QIB5-Meeting-Today
shots.beat: today scene, meeting today: today, catch one “i’m better than that” thought: in traffic, at work, scrolling. don’t argue with it. just name it, and let one person go ahead of you without minding. a saying teaches that whoever humb

films.suffix: a glittering gold-tessera mosaic: small stone and glass tiles, blazing gold ground, deep cobalt and crimson, flat sacred composition

shots.name: QTR1-Garden
shots.beat: God gave Adam and his wife a home: a garden. “Live in it,” He said, “and eat freely from it, wherever you like.”

shots.name: QTR2-Cool-Stream
shots.beat: The Qur’an describes the garden’s promise: no hunger there, no thirst, no going without clothes, no burning sun.

shots.name: QTR3-One-Tree
shots.beat: Then one limit: “Don’t come near this tree, or you will be wrongdoers.” Not even “don’t eat.” Don’t come near.

shots.name: QTR4-Fruit-Branches
shots.beat: Notice what the Qur’an doesn’t say. It doesn’t name the tree, or the fruit. It doesn’t even name his wife. Later tradition calls her Hawwa, Eve.

shots.name: QTR5-Apartment-Today
shots.beat: today scene, apartment today: today, count your garden before the tree. name five things you’re freely given and glad of, before the one thing you can’t have. if you like, end with alhamdulillah.

shots.name: QTR6-Cupboard-Today
shots.beat: today scene, cupboard today: today, count your garden before the tree. name five things you’re freely given and glad of, before the one thing you can’t have. if you like, end with alhamdulillah.

shots.name: QWS1-Night-Garden
shots.beat: In the garden, with everything given and one tree held back, someone began to talk. Not with a shout. With a whisper.

shots.name: QWS2-Leaves-Stir
shots.beat: “Then Shaytan whispered to them,” the Qur’an says. The Arabic is waswasa. Say it slowly: was-was. The word itself whispers.

shots.name: QWS3-Tree-Glowing
shots.beat: He didn’t say “disobey God.” He renamed the tree: the tree of forever, a kingdom that never wears out. And he swore he was their sincere adviser.

shots.name: QWS4-Fallen-Leaves
shots.beat: They both ate. At once they saw their nakedness, and began covering themselves with leaves of the garden.

shots.name: QWS5-Night-Room-Today
shots.beat: today scene, night room today: today, when a nagging voice starts up, ask it one question: is that mine? if you like, say the short refuge many muslims use: a‘udhu billah, i seek refuge in God. or listen to an-nas, the last surah,

shots.name: QWS6-Dawn-Window-Today
shots.beat: today scene, dawn window today: today, when a nagging voice starts up, ask it one question: is that mine? if you like, say the short refuge many muslims use: a‘udhu billah, i seek refuge in God. or listen to an-nas, the last surah

films.suffix: a claymation stop-motion set: handmade plasticine figures and props with visible fingerprints, miniature practical set, soft studio light, shallow depth of field

shots.name: QTB1-Garden-Dusk
shots.beat: After the whisper, Adam and his wife stood in the garden, covered in leaves. And their Lord called to them.

shots.name: QTB2-Fork-Path
shots.beat: This was their fork in the road. Remember Iblis? When he was sent away, he blamed God: “Because You led me astray.”

shots.name: QTB3-Light-Falls
shots.beat: They said: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You don’t forgive us and have mercy on us, we will be lost.”

shots.name: QTB4-Camel-Found
shots.beat: A saying adds a picture: God is happier at a person’s return than a traveler who lost his camel in the desert, then finds it standing right there.

shots.name: QTB5-Kitchen-Sorry-Today
shots.beat: today scene, kitchen sorry today: today, say three hard words about one small thing: “i was wrong.” to a friend, a partner, a coworker, or quietly to God. many muslims say astaghfirullah, i ask God’s forgiveness, through the day.

films.suffix: a woodblock print: carved line texture, two or three flat colours, visible wood grain in the ink, strong black silhouettes, one hot red accent

shots.name: QCR1-Two-Offerings
shots.beat: Now the story comes down to earth, and the first thing it shows is a family. Two sons of Adam each bring an offering to God.

shots.name: QCR2-Light-On-One
shots.beat: One offering is accepted. The other isn’t. And the brother whose offering was refused says: “I will kill you.”

shots.name: QCR3-Staff-Laid-Down
shots.beat: His brother answers: “God accepts only from the mindful. Even if you raise your hand to kill me, I won’t raise mine to kill you.”

shots.name: QCR4-Crow
shots.beat: The Qur’an says simply: his soul talked him into it, and he took his brother’s life. Then God sent a crow, scratching gently at the earth.

shots.name: QCR5-Hill-At-Night
shots.beat: Watching it, he learned how to lay his brother in the earth. “Woe is me!” he cried. “Couldn’t I even be like this crow?” And he was full of regret.

shots.name: QCR6-First-Aid-Today
shots.beat: today scene, first aid today: today, take one small step toward saving a life: look up a first-aid class near you, learn where the nearest defibrillator is, or check in on someone who’s been quiet lately. one life is like all live
